subtopics.name: Nuclear effective field theory and few-body systems
subtopics.scope: Pionless and chiral effective-field-theory descriptions of nuclear forces, applied to two-, three- and four-nucleon bound states, scattering and universal low-energy behavior.

subtopics.name: Shell model and exactly solvable models
subtopics.scope: Configuration-interaction descriptions of nuclei, and schematic solvable Hamiltonians (pairing, seniority, Lipkin-type) used to benchmark many-body approximations.

subtopics.name: Nuclear density functionals and mean-field theory
subtopics.scope: Skyrme, Gogny and relativistic mean-field energy density functionals for ground-state properties, deformation and giant resonances across the nuclear chart.

subtopics.name: Collective motion: geometric and algebraic models
subtopics.scope: Bohr-Mottelson geometric collective Hamiltonians, interacting boson models and dynamical symmetries describing vibrational, rotational and transitional nuclear spectra.

subtopics.name: Dense matter equation of state and neutron stars
subtopics.scope: The equation of state of nuclear and quark matter at high density, and what it implies for neutron-star structure, tidal deformability, cooling and superfluidity.

subtopics.name: Nuclear reaction and scattering theory
subtopics.scope: Optical-model, coupled-channels, R-matrix, eikonal and breakup descriptions of elastic, inelastic, transfer and fusion reactions.

subtopics.name: Radioactive decay, fission and barrier penetration
subtopics.scope: Alpha decay, cluster and proton emission, and fission treated as quantum tunneling through nuclear potential barriers, including half-life systematics.

subtopics.name: Thermonuclear reaction rates and nucleosynthesis
subtopics.scope: Theory of low-energy astrophysical reaction rates, plasma screening and network freeze-out, which underlie big-bang, stellar, s-process and r-process nucleosynthesis.

subtopics.name: Weak interactions and fundamental symmetries in nuclei
subtopics.scope: Beta decay, neutrinoless double-beta decay, neutrino-nucleus interactions, and symmetry-violating observables such as electric dipole moments in nuclear systems.

subtopics.name: Relativistic hydrodynamics of heavy-ion collisions
subtopics.scope: Ideal and viscous relativistic fluid dynamics, its kinetic-theory foundations and attractor behavior, applied to the expanding quark-gluon plasma.

subtopics.name: Hard probes and heavy quarks in QGP
subtopics.scope: Jet energy loss, heavy-quark diffusion and quarkonium dissociation as probes of the hot medium created in nuclear collisions.

subtopics.name: QCD phase diagram and chiral transition
subtopics.scope: Effective-model and field-theory studies of the chiral and deconfinement transitions, the critical point, and color superconductivity at finite temperature and density.

subtopics.name: Hadron spectroscopy and exotic hadrons
subtopics.scope: Quark-model, heavy-quark-symmetry and hadronic-molecule descriptions of meson and baryon spectra, including tetraquark and pentaquark candidates.

subtopics.name: Partonic structure of nucleons and nuclei
subtopics.scope: Parton distributions, form factors, generalized and transverse-momentum-dependent distributions, nuclear modifications and small-x saturation.

techniques.name: EFT matching, power counting and loops
techniques.scope: Build effective Lagrangians, order contributions by power counting, and evaluate loop integrals in dimensional regularization to get amplitudes, low-energy constants or corrections at a fixed order.

techniques.name: Renormalization group flow and fixed points
techniques.scope: Derive and solve Wilsonian, functional or similarity renormalization-group equations for couplings to find fixed points, critical exponents, running behavior or limit cycles.

techniques.name: Effective-range expansion and partial-wave analysis
techniques.scope: Decompose scattering amplitudes into partial waves and extract phase shifts, scattering lengths, effective ranges, pole positions or finite-volume energy shifts.

techniques.name: Self-consistent mean field and BCS
techniques.scope: Use variational Hartree-Fock and BCS/Bogoliubov treatments to obtain gap equations, self-consistency conditions, and closed-form energies or critical values.

techniques.name: Random phase approximation and linear response
techniques.scope: Linearize the equations of motion around a ground state to compute collective excitation energies, strength functions, energy-weighted sum rules or response functions.

techniques.name: Group theory and angular-momentum algebra
techniques.scope: Use Lie-algebra Casimirs, dynamical symmetries, and Clebsch-Gordan and Racah recoupling to get spectra, selection rules and transition ratios exactly.

techniques.name: WKB and semiclassical barrier penetration
techniques.scope: Use semiclassical quantization and tunneling integrals to obtain penetrabilities, half-lives, Gamow factors and Bohr-Sommerfeld spectra.

techniques.name: Hyperspherical and Faddeev three-body methods
techniques.scope: Reduce three-body problems in hyperspherical coordinates, or through Faddeev equations, to transcendental equations for scaling exponents, bound-state energies or recombination rates.

techniques.name: Finite-temperature field theory and resummation
techniques.scope: Use Matsubara sums, hard-thermal-loop resummation and thermal self-energies to compute screening masses, damping rates, pressures and the correlators behind transport coefficients.

techniques.name: Kinetic theory and analytic hydrodynamic solutions
techniques.scope: Solve Boltzmann equations in the relaxation-time approximation or in moment expansions, and construct symmetric flow solutions, to derive transport coefficients, attractors and relaxation rates.

techniques.name: Dispersion relations and sum rules
techniques.scope: Use analyticity, unitarity and the operator product expansion to derive dispersive representations, sum rules and bounds on spectral quantities.

techniques.name: Factorization and QCD evolution equations
techniques.scope: Apply collinear, TMD or small-x factorization with DGLAP, BFKL or BK evolution, Mellin moments and anomalous dimensions to obtain scaling laws and asymptotic forms.
